BACONG PUJPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO. JUL 04 HON. PETER M. UNABIA Governor Province of Misamis Oriental Provincial Capitol Building, Provincial Capitol Compound A Velez St., Cagayan de Oro City Dear Governor Unabia: This has reference to your letter dated May 9, 2024, requesting this Department's legal opinion conceming the recent demise of one of the Sangguniang Panlungsod Members in the City of El Salvador. As represented, the said request arose from the vacancy caused by the demise of the late Sangguniang Panlungsod Member, who was a member of the Centrist Democratic Party (CDP). Apparently, the members of the same political party are allegedly making moves to nominate and appoint a certain person as the successor to the vacant position caused by the death of the late Sangguniang Panlungsod Member. In particular, hereunder are the queries propounded: I. 2. 3. 4. Is there a minimum year of membership for the successor to be effectively considered a member of a political party? Does the requirement of maintaining the basic qualifications for elective office (i.e., the I-year residence requirement and Filipino citizenship) apply to the rules of automatic succession for a successor to ascent to the vacant position? If the continuing qualification requirement applies, can the successor consider his years of residence subsequent to appointment as compliance with the I-year residency required under the law? and What is the reckoning period of the one-year residency requirement insofar as substitutes/nominees for vacant local elective positions are concemed? Shall it be reckoned from the date of the appointment of the substitute, or is there another reckoning point? Foremost, the importance of ensuring that individuals assuming public office fully adhere to the qualifications set forth under the law and is free from any disqualifications cannot be overemphasized—it is paramount to upholding the integrity of govemment institutions. Having stated the foregoing, we shall now address the foregoing issues in seriatim. On the first query, the legal framework goveming vacancies and succession in the local govemment is found in Chapter II of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 (hereinafter referred to as the Code). In the case of the sangguniang members, Section 45 of the Code is instructive, thus: "Section 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian. - "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

(a) Permanent vacancies in the sanggunian where automatic succession provided above do not apply shall be filled by appointment in the following manner: (I) The President, through the Executive Secretary, in the case of the sangguniang panlalawigan and the sangguniang panlungsod of highly urbanized cities and independent component cities; (2) The governor, in the case of the sangguniang panlungsod of component cities and the sangguniang bayan; (3) The city or municipal mayor, in the case of sangguniang barangay, upon recommendation of the sangguniang barangay concerned. (b) Except for the sangguniang barangay, only the nominee Of the political party under which the sanggunian member concemed had been elected and whose elevation to the position next higher in rank created the last vacancy in the sanggunian shall be appointed in the manner hereinabove provided. The appointee shall come from the same political party as that of the sanggunian member who caused the vacancy and shall serve the unexpired term of the vacant office. In the appointment herein mentioned, a nomination and a certificate of membership of the appointee from the hiqhest official of the political party concerned are conditions sine qua non. and any appointment without such nomination and certification shall be null and void ab initio and shall be a ground for administrative action aqainst the official responsible therefore. (c) In case or permanent vacancy is caused by a sanggunian member who does not belong to any political party, the local chief executive shall, upon recommendation of the sanggunian concerned, appoint a qualified person to fill the vacancy. (d) In case of vacancy in the representation of the youth and the barangay in the sanggunian, said vacancy shall be filled automatically by the official next in rank of the organization concemed." (Emphasis supplied) Notably, the Code is primarily concerned with the political stability of local govemment operations. The aforequoted provision explicitly provides that the substitute for the vacant position in the office of the sanggunian must come from the same political party as the sanggunian who vacated the position. The Code is silent as to the duration or the minimum number of years of membership in a political party for a substitute or the successor to be considered a member of a political party. It bears emphasizing that the primary consideration under the Code is that the successor must come from the same political party as the predecessor to ensure consistency in govemance. At any rate, political parties generally have their own by-laws governing their membership, which may include the conditions and stipulations of the minimum period required for their membership. Going now to the second query, we answer in the affirmative. This Department submits that the requirements of maintaining basic qualifications for local elective office, as provided under Section 39 of the Codel and other relevant laws, shall apply Section 39. Qualifications. - (a) An elective local official must be a citizen of the Philippines; a registered voter in the barangay, municipality, city. or province or, in the case of a member of the Sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sangguniang bayan, the district where he intends to be elected; a resident therein for at least one (1) year immediately preceding the day of the election; and able to read and write Filipino Or any other local language or dialect. in the rules of automatic succession. Under the said Section, among the basic prerequisites are, among other things: (I) Filipino citizenship; and (2) at least one (1) year of residency in the locality before the election, among other things. Such qualifications must be upheld throughout their term. This is precisely the clear import of the pronouncement made by the Supreme Court in Maquiling v. COMELEC. The Court ratiocinated that: "Qualifications for public office are continuing requirements and must be possessed not only at the time of appointment or election or assumption of office but during the officer's entire tenure. Once any of the required qualifications is lost, his title may be seasonably challenged. Xxx The citizenship requirement for elective public office is a continuing one. It must be possessed not just at the time of the renunciation of the foreign citizenship but continuously. Any act which violates the oath of renunciation opens the citizenship issue to attack." (Emphasis ours) As to the we likewise answer in the affirmative. This Department opines that the successor may take into account his years of residence subsequent to his appointment in adherence to the I-year residency requirement. Coming now to the last query, while the Code did not clearly delineate the reckoning period of the I-year residency requirement vis-å-vis the nominees or substitutes to fill in the vacancy in the sanggunian, logic dictates that the reckoning period for the 1- year residency requirement should be from the date of the vacancy or the date of assumption to office. This, in our opinion, guarantees that the nominee has been a resident of the locality for at least one year prior to assumption of office. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, SE uthority of the Secretary: R R. LLAMAS cretary for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affairs JVULLLS/LRALLD0am DIR. WILHELM M. SUYKO, CESO IV Regional Director, DILG-X (Northem Mindanao) Masterson Ave., Km. 8, Upper Carmen Cagayan de Oro City (b) Candidates for the position of govemor, vice-govemor, or member of the Sangguniang panlalawigan, or mayor, vice-mayor or member of the sangguniang panlungsod of highly urbanized cities must be at least twenty-one (21 ) years of age on election day. (c) Candidates for the position of mayor or vice-mayor of independent component cities, component cities, or municipalities must be at least twenty-one (21 ) years of age on election day. (d) Candidates for the position Of member Of the sangguniang or sangguniang bayan must be at least eighteen (18) years of age on election day. (e) Candidates for the position of punong barangay or member of the sangguniang barangay must be at least eighteen (18) years of age on election day. (f) Candidates for the sangguniang kabataan must be at least fifteen (15) years of age but not more than twenty-one (21 ) years Of age on election day. 2 G.R. No. 195649, dated April 16, 2023.
